analogs.covers: Society: matriarch with route memory, shared calf care, bulls living apart and a seasonal testosterone surge
Bull temper: attacks anything that comes near the herd and can turn on calves

headline: An Asian elephant matriarchy whose bulls carry a hippo bull's temper.

setting.label: Nomad between courtship and nesting grounds in forest and hill country
setting.note: The matriarch leads migrations from the courtship grounds to the nesting grounds along memorised routes. A bull that owns a herd guards 5 body lengths around it.

playsLike: Cows live in matriarchies of up to 12, led by an experienced matriarch who remembers the routes, and raise calves together. Bulls live apart in sparring bull groups or bonded pairs and win a herd through 1v1 bullfights that the matriarch judges. Only 2 engage in any fight. Small predators are ignored, but a herd bull charges anything that comes within 5 body lengths of his herd, and he gets worse in the rainy season.

why.text: 'Powerful memories and memorized migration paths', with the matriarch at the centre. That is an elephant family (official inspiration: Asian elephants).
Cows practise allomothering, communal calf raising in which every female helps, as elephant herds do.
Bulls live in sparring bull groups or bonded pairs and join cows only when calves are Juvenile or older, like elephant bulls.
Bulls flush with testosterone in the rainy season and fight harder, comparable to an elephant bull in musth.
A herd bull attacks any species within 5 body lengths and may kill calves if they aren't introduced properly. Hippo bulls are notorious for both (official inspiration).

notLike: Elephants have no horns; Eotriceratops fights with horned charges, rhino-style.
Hippos live in water; Eotriceratops is fully terrestrial.
